subject: hydra
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: five-headed hydra.
Style: God of War.
reasoning:
I'm envisioning a five-headed hydra in a God of War aesthetic—dark, scarred, rune-etched, with a massive body, four legs, a tail, and five separate long necks ending in individual heads, starting from the skeleton in a resting pose. I need to make sure the code is solid since I won't be able to test it directly, so I'm planning the structure carefully before building it out.

I'm settling on a scale of a few meters, with the hydra centered at the origin facing forward, and deciding on the color palette: dark slate-green scales, charcoal, bone plates with Nordic runes, ember-orange glowing eyes and cracks, plus battle-worn details like broken chains, a rusted collar, and an embedded broken weapon in its back. Now I'm starting to lay out the skeleton, beginning with a pelvis root joint and a spine chain running from the hips through the body.

Still working on the skeleton: I'm adding a tapering tail chain ending in a bone-spiked tip, then placing the four legs using IK, with front legs more bear-like in proportion and hind legs slightly more digitigrade, tuning joint positions and bend directions so the stance reads as sturdy and powerful.

For front legs with two lengths I just need three names so the chain still gets a tip joint, same logic as before. Now I'm figuring out the feet: a flattened pad box near the floor with toes as small forward-pointing rods tipped with claw spikes, all bound to the ankle/wrist joint, keeping the pad's bottom right at ground level for contact.

Now I'm planning the five necks branching from the chest: bases spread along the shoulder region fanning outward, each a six-joint chain parented to the last spine joint, with heads ending up at varied heights and facing directions to keep the rest pose spread out and visually distinct.

For the jaws, I'm deciding to build the lower jaw geometry first, then apply a small posed rotation (~12°) around the hinge axis afterward so each head reads as subtly open rather than fully closed.

Working through the rotation math, I figure positive rotation about world +X tips the forward vector downward, so local +X would need to map to world −X to get that effect — meaning I should use the jaw joint's dir() with [-1,0,0] to generalize correctly across differently-oriented heads, though I'm not fully certain this holds for all cases.

Actually, to avoid relying on uncertain rotation signs, I decide it's safer to skip posing the jaw entirely and instead build the jaw geometry already open — constructing it directly in model space using offsets from the head's forward and downward directions computed through the head frame, so the open-mouth shape is baked into the geometry rather than achieved through a risky rotation.

Working out the local axis convention: with aim-based quaternion, forward maps to Z, up to Y, and left to X, so I can build each head's geometry in a consistent local frame and place parts via rotated offsets. I'm sketching a HeadFrame helper to handle this placement logic.

Now I'm working out the head structure: a skull as a scaled ellipsoid offset from the neck joint, and a snout built from tapered frustum boxes running forward from the skull.

For teeth, instead of adding a dozen individual cone parts per jaw per head (which balloons the part count across five heads), I'm merging each jaw's teeth into a single geometry per head, keeping just two merged parts for upper and lower teeth.

I'm working out the jaw joint position and using a low-poly faceted cone style for a stylized toothy look. Now moving to the lower jaw geometry, built as a frustum shape hinged at the jaw joint so it can open.

Then I need to define the jaw's local orientation by rotating the head's quaternion around the X axis by the open angle, so the jaw tips downward correctly when opened, and set up the jaw joint with its hinge position, aim direction, and up vector. Finally, I'm setting up the head joint itself, aimed along the forward direction at the end of the neck chain.

For the neck, I want five spans from six Catmull-Rom points, matching one joint name per span so the head joint becomes a child of the last neck joint. Then I'm sweeping the neck chain with a tapering radius from 0.26 to 0.17, applying a dark green paint with lighter countershading on the underside.

Now I'm adding bony spines along the neck's dorsal ridge, placing spike elements at intervals along the sweep's top surface so they follow the neck's curve naturally.

For scars and runes, I'm considering decals rather than extra geometry — placing a rune glyph on the chest plate and a few scar marks on a head, using surface points and normals from the sweep to orient each decal correctly.

Now I'm planning the texture set, aiming for 5-12 total, starting with an ember-slit eye texture. I'm weighing whether to apply it via decal on the skull part versus a separate small flattened ellipsoid shape, leaning toward decals placed near the surface with the outward normal as direction for a cleaner result.

I'm reasoning through decal placement on each side of the skull using mirrored side directions, then wrapping the decal in a glow effect since the eye should be self-luminous. I'm also double-checking that decaling onto a rigid skull part won't cause skin-weight issues since it's not part of a deforming mesh, so it should be safe.

Now I'm planning additional surface details: a chest plate with glowing Elder Futhark rune glyphs drawn as simple stroke paths rather than relying on font rendering, a scar decal with stitch marks for the neck or flank, torus-based chain links with alternating rotation for a chain effect, and a glowing cracked texture for the belly or flank.

I want crack lines in ember orange rendered as a transparent SVG decal with a glow, giving a "chest furnace" look with lava-like veins along the flanks. I'm also considering a Kratos-style red war-paint stripe decal across the central head's face for a distinctive mark.

For texture inventory I'm settling on eye, rune, scar, crack, and war-paint textures, maybe adding a glowing ember mouth interior, plus base materials like scale hide, belly, bone, and iron. I'm weighing whether to import metal and glow helpers from the clockwork/glow kits to save effort versus writing my own paint logic, given some uncertainty about the exact import paths.

Now I'm planning the body structure: lofting skin along a spine chain rooted at the pelvis, with separate chains for spine segments and tail, using catmull curves and careful joint placement to support the quadruped frame with tail.

I'm deciding whether to loft the whole body as one mesh with bone list [tail, pelvis, spine], tapering the tail end to a point, or instead sweep the tail separately along its own chain and loft just the torso along the spine, letting the ends overlap.

I'll just bone the body to the spine chain, since the rear geometry naturally skins to spine1 anyway. Now I'm assigning roles to each joint group — spine, tail, leg, neck, head, jaw — and sketching out the body loft stations with width, height, and y-offset values along the z-axis to define the torso silhouette.

I'm working out how the hips, chest, and shoulder region stack vertically, figuring the chest top sits around y2.5 with neck bases emerging near y2.3 where the five hydra necks will root from a shoulder mound — likely needing an extra ellipsoid or loft shape layered over the main body to bulk out that area.

Now I'm spacing the five neck bases evenly across the shoulder mound, assigning each a position along the x-axis and planning different heights, lengths, and curve paths for each neck to avoid a uniform, repetitive look.

Defining positions for the remaining necks (3 and 4) and sketching a parametric curve approach for S-shaped necks, blending base position, lateral spread, and height using interpolation across six control points per neck.

I'll derive the head direction from the neck's end tangent, nudged downward and slightly outward so it reads as a natural droop rather than a straight continuation. Then I'm sketching proportions: neck length roughly 3-4m tapering from 0.28 to 0.18 thickness, and a head around 1.1m combining skull and snout.

With body length settled at about 3m, I'm planning the armor details—spiked ridges running along the neck's top (about 7 per neck, multiplied across the hydra's heads) plus pale ventral scute bands defined as flat-colored sectors layered over the scale paint on the sweep geometry.

I'm also working out iron neck collars built from ring points swept into a closed loop, sized relative to each neck's radius at that point, with plans for a broken manacle-and-chain detail on one of the heads.

Now I'm giving each of the four necks its own identity: one scarred with a blinded milky eye and a broken horn, one wearing the iron collar and chain, the center head biggest with a bone crest, war-paint stripe, and glowing brow runes, and the last with a weapon embedded in it — considering a broken spear or axe lodged in the skull for a Kratos-inspired touch.

I'm planning to structure the build as a `buildHead(i, cfg)` function looping over all five necks, each with its own scale, horn type, eye style, and features, keeping the code long but organized. Now I'm working out the color palette — dark olive-grey scale tones with darker crevices, contrasted against a grittier bone-toned belly.

Adding mud and soot blending...

I confirm `resolve` is exported through the SDK's index, so I'll import paint, noise, mix, smoothstep, resolve, scales, mottle, countershade, stripes, gradient, grain, and patches together. Now I'm settling on a limited flat color palette, starting with bone tones and planning a horn gradient that transitions from light bone to dark along its length.

For the horns, I'm mixing a pale ashen base into dark tips using smoothstep on the sweep coordinate, plus adding grain streaks via noise for texture. I'm also setting up iron and bronze metal materials with tarnish, defining ember colors for glow effects, and picking blood-red and deeper tones for the mouth interior with a subtle ember glow inside.

Now I'm starting the imports for the component builder, pulling in geometry merging utilities, the core builder functions, and the glow and metal kits, while checking whether DEG is actually exported from the library.

Setting up the build function and metadata, and reconsidering the paint texture resolution—weighing whether 2048 is too heavy given the model's large surface area and estimating the texel density needed.

Now I'm defining the pelvis as the root spine joint with its position, then building out the spine's curve path through a series of control points.

Defining the chain structure for spine joints...

The chest will reference the last spine joint. Next I'm building the tail chain similarly, with its own curve path extending backward and down, tapering the joints along the way.

Writing tail sweep radius function...

I'm checking the taper looks right near the tail tip and keeps clear of the ground, then I want to cap the end with a distinct bone-like shape — maybe a leaf-shaped blade or a spiked club form.

Now I'm adding a cluster of bone spikes around the tail tip: a main spike extending backward along the tangent plus a ring of smaller angled spikes, and then dorsal spines running along the tail that shrink in size toward the end based on position along the sweep.

Next I'm lofting the main body shape, defining a series of cross-sections with positions, widths, and heights along the spine from tail to head, giving it the hide material.

I'm checking the body proportions against leg placement—the hips sit slightly outside the belly profile, and the stance looks reasonable given the leg lengths. Then I confirm the loft correctly follows the spine bone chain and that painting coordinates align with the loft's parametrization. Now I want to add a shoulder hump where the five necks emerge, using a sphere geometry for the mound.

Next I'm thinking through armor: dorsal spike plates running along the spine using the `along` helper, plus rune-carved bone plates for a God of War-style aesthetic, and large bronze slabs strapped to the shoulders to evoke scavenged armor.

I'm also embedding trophy weapons as detail: broken spears and a hacked axe jammed into the flank and shoulder, with the axe styled like Kratos' Leviathan—icy-blue glowing runes on the blade to contrast against the ember-orange palette. Now moving on to leg construction, starting with the front legs.

Working out shoulder and foot joint positions for a symmetric left/right pair, computing limb reach so the bent-elbow pose looks natural rather than overextended—adjusting segment lengths so the elbow bends backward like a bear's foreleg.

I'm setting up the three-joint chain (shoulder, elbow, hand) with tapering radius values along its length, and considering adding a rounded shoulder plate using a half-sphere geometry for armor detail.

Now I'm sketching out the leg's remaining parts -- a paw sweep, box-shaped foot, toes with claws, an elbow spike, and a spiked pauldron -- and building a helper function to generate the paw geometry from a tip joint and sizing parameters.

Checking the claw tip stays near the ground plane, that works out fine. Now I'm working through the hind legs as three-segment digitigrade limbs, setting hip and foot positions and segment lengths, noting the total reach is longer than the actual distance so the knee bends forward and the hock back, with the last segment ideally running roughly vertical like a cannon bone when the IK hint allows it.

I'm adding a haunch mass as an ellipsoid at the hip, naming the four hind-limb joints, and setting radius tapering keys along the limb. For bend hints, I'm assigning one bend direction per inner joint, giving two directions for the three hind leg segments.

Checking the IK reach for the hind leg, I confirm the hip-to-foot distance is well within the limb's maximum extension. I'm also noting that the limb sweep uses a polyline through the joint points, which should round nicely at corners.

Now I'm starting to define neck configuration objects, setting up properties like base position, offsets, and droop for each named neck variant.

I'm working out neck placement around the mound: five necks spaced across the x-axis, with base points positioned near the mound's surface at consistent height and depth, while checking that neck radii don't cause adjacent necks to overlap at their bases.

Working out the remaining necks: i2 rears straight up tallest, i3 reaches furthest forward, i4 droops lower on the opposite flank—giving varied head heights and a natural fanned-out hydra silhouette. Overall the creature ends up roughly 5m tall, 4.5m wide, and spans about 9m from tail to forward heads—a suitably massive monster.

Now I'm defining the curve for each neck path: it arcs upward and forward using eased interpolation, with a cubic droop term pulling the tip down near the end so heads sag slightly rather than pointing straight out, keeping the base tangent vertical so necks emerge naturally from the body.

I'm also working out the forward direction vector at the curve's tip, adding a slight outward yaw so heads splay apart, then normalizing it and using it to orient each head's up vector before building the actual head geometry.

Setting the local frame origin at the neck joint with forward, up, and left axes, I'm confirming the cross product handedness works out so that +X local correctly maps to world left.

Now I'm sketching out the skull geometry piece by piece: the cranium as a scaled sphere positioned slightly forward, and the brow ridge as angled ellipsoids placed symmetrically above where the eyes will go.

I'm also figuring out the snout shape, planning to use a tapered cylinder with only four radial segments to get a diamond-like cross-section that mimics a wedge, rotated and scaled to fit the overall head proportions.

Actually I should think through a frustumBox helper that takes two points and width/height pairs to build a tapered box section between them, and work out how its orientation should behave—the width axis defaults to staying roughly aligned with world X, which works fine for heads tilted in pitch, but for yawed heads I need the width direction to project correctly relative to the facing direction rather than just staying horizontal.

For construction, I'll use frustumBox for the snout and jaw forms since it suits a blocky puppet style well, and layer in extra details like a nose bump sphere, nostrils, a snout ridge crest, and an upper lip flange for character.

Working out the upper jaw dimensions and the lower jaw hinge placement, defining the frustumBox spans for cranium and snout along z, their width/height tapers, and the pivot point for the jaw's opening angle.

Now I'm sketching the lower jaw geometry as its own frustum box in the jaw's local frame, then setting up a joint for it with a parent-child link to the head, an aim target, and an up direction to define its rotation role.

For the mouth interior, I'm adding a tongue as a tapered frustum shape, plus a thin palate slab positioned just under the upper jaw's underside to avoid z-fighting, computing the snout's bottom edge coordinates to position it flush.

Now I'm working out the upper teeth placement, interpolating positions along both sides of the snout from front to back, sizing fangs larger toward the front, and using downward-pointing cone geometry rotated to point along the jaw's underside as tooth shapes.

To avoid the forbidden quaternion utility functions, I'm building a helper that computes an orientation from a direction vector using an allowed "aim" method instead, then defining a frame helper class that converts local coordinates to world space by applying the rotation and scale and adding the origin offset.

Now I'm writing a teeth-merging function that builds cone geometries for each tooth, orients and positions them using the frame helper, merges them into a single geometry, and wraps it as a part attached to the appropriate bone.

I'm noting cone geometry normals look smooth by default with 5 sides, and considering adding a `flat: true` option for faceted shading on merged geometries. For horns, I'm planning to use a swept bezier curve along skull points with tapering radii and flat/pointed end caps.

Now I'm thinking through horn variety per head: one with curved swept-back horns where one is broken into a stub, and another using a spiral path for ram-style horns, where I need the spiral's starting point to align with its center.

For geometry that's too risky, I'll switch to a simpler curling bezier using five catmull points instead. For the central head, I'm planning a big crown with a fan of crest spikes arranged in an arc plus a massive pair of swept-back horns.

I'm considering an extruded jagged crest ridge along the head/neck top instead, with six radial bone spikes tilted back around the occiput and two large horns. For variant three I'm thinking antler-style horns with branching tines, each built from a main bezier curve plus two smaller spikes.

Now I'm shifting to armored helmet details: a flat slab plate with big spikes on the forehead, sideways-swept cheek spikes, and a paired set of back-flaring jaw spikes with varied sizes across all variants. I'm also placing the eye decals onto the cranium geometry, positioning them based on head side and orientation vectors.

Adding eye texture details...

I need to figure out the orientation for a side-facing eye — which way is "up" versus the horizontal axis running toward the snout.

Working through the vector math for the left side: with the viewer looking inward along the outward normal and up being +Y, the drawing's rightward direction actually points toward the back of the head, while the front of the head is toward the left of the drawing. So for an angry slant, the inner (front) end needs to sit lower on that side.

For mirroring, the left eye (s=+1) stays unmirrored while the right eye (s=-1) gets mirrored, keeping the lowered-front-end slant consistent on both sides. I'm checking that the eye position at the chosen local coordinates lands close to the cranium ellipsoid's surface, and the math confirms it's right at about 0.99, so the placement is good.

I'm deciding the decal should target the cranium part, applied after the cranium is created, with the head bone assigned so it deforms rigidly with the skull. For the glowing effect on the eye texture, I'm wrapping the decal in a glow function, since decals produce standard materials compatible with that. For the blind-eye variant, I'm planning a separate milky-white scarred texture without any glow applied.

Now I'm working out placement for a warpaint stripe decal, positioning it near the top of the skull with an upward-angled direction so it doesn't visually clash with the eye decal underneath.

I'm also planning a pale-bone claw scar texture with visible stitches to place across the snout, neck, and body flank.

For the flank placement, I'm figuring out the surface positioning on the loft body—picking an azimuth and elevation around the tube to find a hit point on the left side, then using that hit's surface normal to orient the decal correctly.

I'm also planning glowing ember crack decals for the opposite flank and rune decals across the body plates. Now I'm sketching the eye texture as SVG, layering an almond-shaped outline, a fiery orange iris, and inner highlight shapes to build up the look.

Still writing eye SVG...

Drawing stitch marks over the scars, then sketching the crack network with glowing orange fractures and a hot inner core, checking that stroke widths scale properly at 256px. Now I'm starting on the rune glyphs design.

Still mapping out rune paths...

For the axe blade I'm thinking a flat ice-blue glow extrusion is simplest, maybe adding a rune decal like Tiwaz in a circle as a forehead brand mark, skipping more decorative decals to keep things manageable.

I'm planning texture sets (eyes, blindness, scars, cracks, runes, Tyr brand, warpaint) and paint palettes (hide, bone/horn, iron, bronze, plating) to cover armor and skin variations, then sketching how neck details and chain sweeps should follow a radius curve.

Working on belly band sectors...

I'm planning to reuse the same scute-paint function across neck, body, and tail by parameterizing the frequency, so belly plates appear consistently with mottled bone-tan tones and darker seam lines along the underside.

For the hide base, I'm layering dark scale textures with a cool green-gray palette, then adding subtle ashy highlights toward the top of the body using a smoothstep blend based on surface normal, plus mud staining near the feet.

Still writing paint functions...

Adding helper resolution for nested paints and setting up the tail and limb paint functions, then starting on the shoulder pauldron geometry using a scaled hemisphere for scavenged bronze plates.

I'm defining a panelled bronze metal texture with tarnish and verdigris for the plates, considering rivet rings and spikes on the pauldrons, then moving to dorsal armor plates placed along the back using disc-shaped cylinders stuck to sweep points.

Now I'm placing five plates along the back at varying t positions with spikes mounted on top, merging the plate base and spike into single stations, then adding a broken chain hanging from a collar on the neck.

The chain hangs down with elongated torus links alternating orientation, rigged to follow the neck joint nearest its attachment point so it moves naturally with the body.

I realize the chain might clip through the shoulder mound at that position, so I'm shifting the collar attachment point further along the neck curve to clear it, letting the six links hang freely in front of the chest down to about 0.9m.

Instead I'll give two necks (1 and 3) iron collars with their own broken dangling chains for a "bound hydra broke free" effect, reusing collar and hangChain helpers, while the central neck gets decorative stacked bone vertebra rings with spikes along its length.

I'll go with -30 tilt so the collar sweeps back toward the body like a frill. Skipping a membrane since this is a Greek hydra, I'll keep the neck spikes as is, add ember crack decals on neck 4 and scars on neck 0, then move to embedding broken weapons—starting with a splintered spear shaft piercing the left flank, plus a couple more broken spears in the back.

Adding more weapon placements...

Still shaping the blade outline...

Now I'm adding a back-spike beard blade, grip wrap segments, and pommel for the axe, then working out its exact placement on the shoulder mound using ray-surface intersection to get accurate positioning.

Next I'm figuring out the axe's orientation vectors, tilting it back with a lean, computing the perpendicular "across" direction via cross products so the blade faces correctly toward the front-left, with the cutting edge on the +X side.

Checking placement though, the axe at that position would collide with the neck bases near the top of the mound, so I'm shifting it behind the necks to z=0.35 on the back of the body, then verifying against the body's surface profile to confirm it sits clear of the mound geometry there.

Now I'm working out spear placements using surface-hit directions around the body at different azimuth and elevation angles for left, right, and rear flanks, computing lean directions and shaft endpoints from each hit point.

I need to handle bone attachment for spears riding the body surface, falling back to the chest bone if a hit has no bone data. Then I'm adding ember-glow touches for the fire-breather look—throat glow spheres placed inside the mouths on each head.

I'm placing the throat glow deep under the snout so it only peeks out when the jaw is open, positioning it near the dark red palate box. Next I'm sketching the brow ridge as a thick hide-colored ellipsoid and adding small dark ember nostril bumps.

Adding nostril glow and spikes...

Working through the jaw hinge geometry now, figuring out box dimensions so the lower jaw sits correctly when closed and clears the snout bottom when opened at 14 degrees, checking the gap at the front tip versus the back.

Positioning lower teeth along the jaw edges with a tusk-like canine near the tip, adding a rounded nose cap to cover the snout's flat end, a jaw tip cap sphere, and starting on the cheek geometry.

I'm now adding spiked frills at the jaw hinge using explicit bone references, applying bone parameters consistently to the sweeps and frustum boxes, and defining a smaller, darker scale-pattern paint for the head region.

For the head I'm layering a countershaded belly tone underneath the scale pattern, varying head size, eye type, and horn style per creature id, and confirming the neck chain's default roll is fine before setting up the head joint parented to the last neck segment.

I'm making sure the head joint parent, direction, and up-vector align with where the neck chain ends, since the neck sweep's rounded cap extends slightly past the path end into the head, and I'm defining the neck path points running from base to head so the whole chain sweeps as one smooth continuous mesh.

I'm adding spike-based armor along the neck sweep, placing them so the dorsal ridge sits on the back side when the neck rises vertically and shifts to the top once the neck turns horizontal, keeping the spikes tapering smaller toward the head.

Now I'm sketching out the per-head building function and supporting types, setting up a list of head definitions and vector helpers so I can place parts using Vector3 coordinates directly.

Writing SVG code...

I'm deciding to target the decal across both cranium and snout parts, projecting the grid downward onto whichever surface it hits first, sized to run along the centerline from skull top to nose.

I'm placing a snout-side decal by positioning it along the head's x-axis with an outward-tilted direction, then working through runes along the neck — aligning the texture's row direction with the neck's tangent and figuring out which way "up" should point relative to that sweep.

That confirms the math works out so that right equals the tangent vector, which is what I need for orienting decals along the curve. Now I'm checking the neck decal dimensions against the curved surface segments to make sure the resolution is fine enough, and deciding to keep decal parameters consistent (at, dir, up, size, segments) across all uses to avoid API mismatches that could break the whole module.

Now I'm writing the head-building function, computing the tangent at the end of the neck path, blending in yaw/pitch offsets to get a forward direction, then using that with an up vector to compute an orientation quaternion for placing the head joint.

Writing part helper...

Defining ell and box helpers that wrap unit sphere/box geometries scaled via the part transform. I'm wary of sharing a single geometry instance across parts in case the SDK mutates geometry in place when attaching it to a bone, so I'll create a fresh geometry object for each call instead to stay safe.

Now working through the head's individual features one by one, like the cranium and brow ridges, figuring out how to orient each ellipsoid's long axis and rotation so the brow ridge angles upward toward the outside to convey an angry expression.

Building the snout frustum tapering toward the front, colored with the bone head material, then adding a tip ellipsoid and a small ridge on top for the nose detail.

I'm positioning a dark armored nasal ridge over the snout and adding glowing ember-colored nostril ellipsoids on either side, working out their exact placement relative to the tip's curved surface.

Now I'm generating the upper teeth, looping through left and right sides to compute tooth width, base height, and length as they taper from front to back along the jaw.

Next I'm setting up the jaw joint pivot and rotation quaternion to drive the jaw's opening motion based on the config angle.

Adding jaw geometry next...

Adding more spike variants...

Still working out curl points...

For the center head type, I'm planning two large backward-sweeping horns using a bezier curve with increasing height and backward tilt, plus a crown of five smaller spikes around it.

For the antler type, I'm using a main bezier branch with three tines per side spawning off points along the sweep, oriented along the surface normal so they point mostly upward from the tube.

For the helmet type, I'm planning bull-style forward-curving horns defined by a base, two control points, and a tip, plus a simple bony brow plate box on the forehead decorated with a TYR rune decal.

I also want to vary eye configs per head—ember as default, with head 0 being blind—and add neck decals like ember cracks with glow on one neck sweep and scars on another. Now I'm ready to write the final TypeScript module, starting with the imports and geometry merging setup.

Defining the bone-themed color palette...

Still shaping body geometry...

Now moving to the leg structure, defining a helper for feet placement and looping through left and right sides to build front and back legs symmetrically.

Confirming the chest joint position lines up with the shoulder attachment point, then working out the sweep radius profile for the forelimb—tapering from shoulder to wrist with a slight elbow bulge—while checking the lower end radius doesn't clip through the floor at the foot contact point.

Now I'm designing the pauldron as a hemisphere dome geometry placed at the shoulder, tilted outward from the body with a rotation that flips based on left or right side.

Placing the spike at the dome top with verified coordinates, plus two smaller flanking spikes, then moving on to a forearm cuff ring.

I'm designing a reusable cuff helper that builds a ring of points around a chain location and sweeps a pentagon-sided tube through them to form a broken manacle, sized around a radius of 0.215, planning to apply it to both forelegs with a trailing broken chain effect.

Now I'm moving on to the hind legs, placing a haunch using an ellipsoid at the hip positioned to overlap the body's width at that z-depth, then defining the hind limb joints with specific coordinates and axis orientations for the leg segments.

Adding tail spikes...

Building out the neck chain loop...

I'm adding ruff spikes around neck 2 and planning decals for the other necks—scars on neck 0, a stitched wound, and cracks on neck 4. For the decals I need a helper that projects textures onto the sweep surface using the point's normal, tangent, and computed up vector, with runes oriented along the tangent direction.

For scars I'll orient along the tangent since any slash direction works, and I'm keeping cracks and scars using their own colored textures rather than tinting. Now I'm placing body decals—cracks on the flank using a surface hit around a chest point, and a glowing ember wound near the front of the chest.

Adjusting flank scar positions on both sides with different azimuths and sizes, making sure the crack decals explicitly use the hit normal for direction. For the rune decals on the left flank, I'm working out the up vector by crossing the hit normal with a reference axis so the runes align properly along the body surface.

Confirming that orientation works correctly for a creature facing +X, so text reads rear-to-front naturally. Now I'm moving to the spear construction helper, defining a function that takes a hit point, normal, and bone reference to build the spear geometry along a given direction and length.

Writing spear rod and spike geometry...

Computing axe geometry now: raycasting for placement, combining the body and mound into a surface, then working out the perpendicular "across" vector via a cross product so the blade extends properly in the X direction, and setting the haft base position relative to the axe's hit point.

Defining axe blade geometry...

Defining color palettes and shading functions...

Good, the smoothstep direction checks out against the verdigris example, and mix accepting Rgb types is fine. Now I'm defining a scute paint function with a mottled texture and angle-based skin tone logic...

Still writing head scale paint...

Now I'm setting up plate, iron, and steel material textures, then defining a helper class for attaching things to bones with position and orientation tracking relative to a joint.

Still defining helper methods...

Finishing the teeth merge function...

Now I'm defining the head config type with knob size, jaw opening, yaw/pitch, horn count, and blind-eye flag, then starting buildHead to compute orientation by combining the path's end tangent with yaw/pitch offsets and aiming it against a reference axis.

Adding eye decals, checking for blindness and applying a glow effect, with size ratios matching the texture's aspect.

I'm verifying the decal projection direction works outward correctly for each eye, then moving to brow shaping and horn construction per type via a switch statement. Now I'm setting up the helmet plate decal for head 4, positioning the TYR texture on a bone-colored plate.

Still working out box geometry sizing...

Now I'm adding decal details: a glowing ember mark on one head, warpaint across the center head's top, and scar decals on the side heads using a snout sweep as the surface target. I'm also sketching a throat glow element positioned beneath the jaw.
